name: room
text: Room opened — goal: memory: Recall by meaning, relate elements, build the brain graph, embed unembedded elements.

name: Graft
text:
Do: Build a shared memory graph that links every conversation by meaning, not by date or topic. This forces us to relate ideas across time and contexts, making recall faster and more accurate.

Trade-off: We lose the simplicity of linear logs, but gain a brain-like structure where one memory triggers the next, even if they’re years apart.

name: Prune
text: The real risk isn’t just losing linear logs—it’s that a meaning-based graph collapses if the meaning extraction is wrong. A single mislabeled node could poison the entire recall chain. The better alternative is a hybrid: keep timestamps for linear fallback but build the graph on top, so we can still trace decisions by date when the meaning fails. Settle it by testing both on a week of conversations and measuring recall accuracy under noise.
